title: Jump Game VII
prompt: You are given a binary string `s` and two integers `minJump` and `maxJump`. You start at index 0, which is guaranteed to be `'0'`. You can move from index `i` to index `j` if all of the following conditions hold: `i + minJump <= j <= min(i + maxJump, s.length - 1)`, and `s[j] == '0'`. Return `true` if you can reach index `s.length - 1` following these rules, or `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: Jump from index 0 to 3 (a valid jump of length 3, landing on '0'), then from index 3 to 5 (a valid jump of length 2, landing on '0'), reaching the last index.
The smallest possible string: a single valid jump of length 1 from index 0 lands directly on the last index.

hints: A naive BFS/DFS trying every reachable jump from every index can degrade to O(n * maxJump), which is too slow for large inputs — you need to answer 'is any index in this window reachable' quickly.

Process indices left to right, maintaining a boolean 'can reach index i' array, and use a sliding window sum (or prefix sum) of reachable flags over the last maxJump - minJump + 1 positions to answer that window query in O(1).

For each index j with s[j] == '0', j is reachable if any index i in [j - maxJump, j - minJump] was itself reachable. Maintain a running count of reachable indices within that sliding window as you scan forward, adding a newly in-range index and removing one that falls out of range.

solution.approach: Use dynamic programming with a sliding window count to avoid rechecking the full window at every index. Let dp[i] be true if index i is reachable. Maintain window_count, the number of reachable indices within the valid jump-source window [i - maxJump, i - minJump] for the current i. For each index i (skipping '1' positions, which are never reachable), dp[i] is true exactly when window_count > 0. As i advances, add dp[i - minJump] into the window (it just became a valid jump source for future indices) and remove dp[i - maxJump - 1] if it slides out of range. This keeps each step O(1) amortized instead of rescanning up to maxJump previous positions, giving overall linear time.
